subtype: Work, family and personal duties colliding [Actor]
passage: I'm Samir, and I sit two desks from Reena. For a month I've noticed Reena staying past seven to finish the quarterly deck, then taking a call in the corridor. Reena's parents want to fix a date for a relative's ceremony and expect Reena to travel for the whole week. On Monday, Reena said sorry to the manager, and on Tuesday said sorry to a parent on the phone in nearly the same voice. Reena's eyes looked tired but the smile stayed polite. I can't tell what exactly Reena feels; maybe guilt about both, maybe resentment too. On Friday I heard, “I love them, and I'm also so cross with them,” said to nobody in particular.

qa.q: How long had Samir noticed Reena staying late?
qa.a: Samir had noticed Reena staying past seven for a month.

qa.q: What might Reena be feeling when saying “I love them, and I'm also so cross with them”?
qa.a: Reena seems to feel love and resentment together, guilty about neglecting either work or family, and neither feeling cancels the other.

qa.q: What could Reena try to ease the collision of demands?
qa.a: Tell the manager and the parents which days can actually be given, so neither side is silently disappointed.

qa.q: How does Samir interpret Reena's polite smile?
qa.a: Samir sees it as a cover for tiredness, but admits guessing, since Samir cannot see Reena's real feelings.

grounding: A young professional balances a demanding job with parents' expectations and feels guilty about whichever is neglected.

subtype: Work, family and personal duties colliding [Actor]
passage:
Monday: Sunaina wrote three things on a sticky note: the product launch, Ma's puja on Sunday and the reunion dinner with her old friends. All three looked impossible. Her mother rang twice during the meeting, and Nitin, her team lead, gave her a look when she stepped out.

Thursday: Sunaina stayed late for the launch, missed the call from her mother, then felt guilty and ordered nothing for dinner.

Sunday: She reached the puja an hour late, left before the prasad, and half-listened during the dinner. She felt guilty about each thing, and a little resentful about all of them, and both feelings sat together in her chest.

qa.q: What three things did Sunaina write on the sticky note?
qa.a: Sunaina wrote the product launch, Ma's puja on Sunday and the reunion dinner with old friends.

qa.q: How did Sunaina feel on Sunday, and how do we know?
qa.a: Sunaina felt guilty and resentful together: she was late, left early and half-listened, and both feelings sat in her chest.

qa.q: What could Sunaina do earlier in the week to make Sunday less of a collision?
qa.a: Tell her mother, Nitin and her friends which parts she can attend, and agree what will be shortened, rather than hoping to manage all three.

qa.q: How might Nitin see Sunaina stepping out of the meeting?
qa.a: Nitin, as team lead, probably notices the interruption and may feel concerned or impatient, without knowing the calls are about the puja.

grounding: A young professional balancing work, family and friends feels guilty about whichever is neglected, with resentment alongside duty.
